main_text.p: essem minor, legebam coram Rabbi Iehuda in volumine Esther, isque erat ager. Quod vero projectus in solo dabat illi operam ad pedes ejus, probatur sententia Iosé ben Iochezer in Pirke Avoth: יהי ביתך בית ועד לחכמין והוי מתאבק בעפר רגליהם Sit domus tua domus conciliabuli Sapientibus, & pulveriza te pulvere pedum eorum. & eo loco Pauli Act. 22 3. ἀνατεθραμμένος ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ παρὰ τοὺς πόδας Γαμαλιήλ. Quamdiu erat בחור vocabatur de nomine patris, non addito nomine proprio. Post χειροθεσίαν, dicebatur Rabbi Iosua Ben Bethira. Ante χειροθεσίαν, tacito nomine Iosuae tantum ben Bethira, Eliezer. &c, Postea promovebatur ad Magisterium per manus impositionem, quam Graeci Ecclesiastici χειροθεσίαν, Hebraei Magistri סמיכה vocant: quemadmodum eum qui magistratus est סמוך vocant, aut saltem qui est Mello-doctor.Hac de re. Vide Cunaeum de Rep Ebr. lib. 1. cap. 12. Qui manum imponebat, dicebatur, סומך. Et propterea Rabbi Iuda filius Babae cognominabatur הסומך ὁ χειροθέτης, quia absque eo foret, inquiunt Thalmudistae, actum erat de manuum Impositionis actu legitimo. Ipse enim carmen legitimum τῆς χειροθεσίας instituit.
יהודה בן בבא הסומך שאלמלא היו בטלו דיני קנסות לישראל וכן הסמיכה: והסמיכה לא היתה אלא בידו משה ליהושע אלא אפילו בדבר בלבד די שיאמר אני סומך אותך תהיה כמוך

Magister Iuda filius Babae cognomine χειροθέτης, propterea quod absque eo fuisset, perierant ex Israel77 tam judicia criminalia, quam manuum impositio, quae non fiebat per manum duntaxat, quomodo fecit Moses Iosua, sed & conceptis verbis praeter illud quod dici solet, Ego tibi impono manum & manus impositas tibi esto, hoc est, Et magister esto. Ex quibus colligitur non solum vetustissimam fuisse χειροθεσίας formulam illam, quae ibi concepta est, sed etiam aliud praeterea verborum civilium carmen ad formam

page.notes: Hebrew and Greek passages are transcribed as printed; the Hebrew line of Pirke Avoth and the Hebrew lines following "Iuda" are printed right to left and may contain small errors. The marginal note block beside "Hac de re" is partly illegible at its edges. Note: the "77" and "76" marks are section numbers beside the text. Greek word "ἀνατεθραμμένος" and "παρὰ τοὺς πόδας" are rendered from the scan with uncertainty. The word "formam" is a catchword-like final word at the foot of the column.
